clinical_notes: Patient reports increased breathlessness with moderate exertion. Consider Venturi mask at 28% FiO2 for use during exacerbations.
Patient experiencing increased sputum production and nocturnal dyspnea. Prescribed high-flow nasal cannula for home use with settings at 25L/min, 40% FiO2.
Recent hospitalization for acute exacerbation. Dependent on home BiPAP therapy with settings IPAP 16 EPAP 6. Recommended 15 hours/day usage.
Stable condition. Mild symptoms only with strenuous exercise. No oxygen supplementation required at this time.
Increasing frequency of exacerbations. CAT score 28. Recommended non-rebreather mask during acute episodes with titration to maintain SpO2 > 90%.
Slight improvement with adjusted medication regimen. Continue with Venturi mask at 28% FiO2 as needed for exertional dyspnea.
Significant decline in lung function. 6MWT distance decreased to 150m. Upgraded to BiPAP mask with heated humidification. IPAP 18 EPAP 8.
Well-controlled with current treatment plan. Recommend basic oxygen mask at 2L/min for use during upper respiratory infections only.
No significant change from previous assessment. Continue with high-flow nasal cannula as prescribed.
Reports improved exercise tolerance with pulmonary rehabilitation. Venturi mask 24% FiO2 recommended for use during moderate to severe exacerbations.

Slight improvement in symptoms with aggressive bronchodilator therapy. Continue BiPAP therapy with current settings.

Maintaining stable pulmonary function. No respiratory support indicated at this time.

Slight decline in lung function. Added short-acting bronchodilator as needed. Basic oxygen mask at 2L/min still appropriate for occasional use.
Stable condition. Continuing pulmonary rehabilitation with good results. Maintain current Venturi mask recommendation.
Critical deterioration in lung function. Considering referral for lung transplant evaluation. CPAP with high FiO2 and nasal high-flow during daytime.
Maintaining relatively stable condition. Low-flow nasal cannula during sleep continues to be effective.
Slight decrease in FEV1. Increased inhaled corticosteroid dose. Continue with Venturi mask at 28% FiO2 during exacerbations.
Tolerating high-flow nasal cannula well. Adjusted to 30L/min, 35% FiO2 during exertional activities.
Improvement noted with intensive respiratory therapy program. Can temporarily downgrade from BiPAP to high-flow nasal cannula during daytime hours.
Maintaining stable condition. No respiratory support needed at this time.
Slightly improved SpO2 with medication adjustments. Recommend continuing non-rebreather mask during exacerbations, considering high-flow nasal cannula for home use.
Progressive decline despite optimal medical therapy. BiPAP settings adjusted to IPAP 22 EPAP 10. Consider tracheostomy if further deterioration occurs.
Stable condition. Basic oxygen mask at 2L/min continues to be appropriate for symptomatic relief as needed.
Stable with current treatment regimen. Venturi mask at 24% FiO2 still appropriate for use during exacerbations.
Severe respiratory failure requiring consideration for end-of-life care planning. Total face CPAP mask with highest FiO2 settings and humidification recommended.
